subject: Re: Follow-up: Reranking & embeddings comparison vs hyperscaler
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — quick recap & proposed next tests (rerank/embeddings)

Samir — thanks again for the discovery call today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can validate the trade-offs you care about (latency, recall, and unit cost):

Summary of priorities you shared:
- Reranking pipeline: existing retrieval + lightweight reranker at query time (low latency SLOs, p95 < 200ms).
- Embedding store: cost per vector and recall@k (k=10,100) are top of mind; want to compare recall vs hyperscaler embeddings + egress costs.
- Control over model variants: ability to pin quantized variants for cost/latency testing.

Proposed experiments (what we can run from Redwood quickly):
1) Embedding accuracy sweep: generate embeddings for a 10k doc subset with our open model (6-8 dims variants to test: 512, 768, 1024) vs SearchLytics baseline + AWS/GC embeddings (if you can share a sample or allow us to call theirs). Evaluate recall@10/100 and average cosine distances.
2) Retrieval latency matrix: host the vector index in our dedicated pool and measure cold/hot query p50/p95/p99 across batch sizes (1, 8, 32) and index types (IVF, HNSW). Goal: p95 < 200ms for batch 1; report tail behavior.
3) Reranker latency/cost test: run lightweight transformer reranker (quantized int8) on top-100 candidates; measure per-query token cost and end-to-end latency for rerank+retrieve.

What we need from you to start:
- 10k sample docs (or allow Redwood to sample from your index) + 200 representative queries (we can reuse the sample queries you mentioned).
- Confirmation if we can call your hyperscaler embedding endpoint for a direct apples-to-apples test, or whether you'll run the embedding export and share vectors.

Attached: initial comparison template (searchlytics-compare-table.xlsx) and a sample queries file (rerank-sample-queries.jsonl).

Next steps: if this plan looks good I’ll loop in Dylan (SE) to own the benchmarking script and schedule a 45-min test-run kickoff.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our internal priorities. A few clarifications and constraints from my side:

1) Data sample: we can export a 10k doc sample and the 200 queries; I’ll have that to you by EOD Thursday (2026-03-12). I’ll share via our S3 link (will DM credentials to Ben).
2) Hyperscaler embeddings: we prefer not to grant external calls into our paid embedding endpoint. I can export their vectors for the sample set (they’re using 1024-d on GCP) and share the file — that works for apples-to-apples.
3) Cost metric: please include estimated per-100k-query cost for generating embeddings + storage egress assumptions (we’re comparing total monthly cost if we move to Redwood).

One more ask: what’s the vector dimensionality sweet spot you typically recommend for Recall vs cost? We saw diminishing returns above 768 on our initial tests but want the careful benchmark.

Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@searchlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap & proposed next tests (rerank/embeddings)

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few technical notes and an initial recommendation: 

On vector dims: empirical guidance from our benchmarks — for dense retrieval on 10k docs: 512 -> baseline recall@10 reasonable; 768 -> noticeable uplift; 1024 -> marginal gains for many corpora but useful when queries are semantically distant. Given your note about diminishing returns, I’d propose testing 512, 768, 1024 but focus on 768 as the likely sweet spot.

On latency and index types:
- HNSW: best p50/p95 for mid-sized indexes, but memory cost is higher.
- IVF with re-ranking: lower memory and steady recall when combined with a strong reranker.

Reranker strategy:
- Top-100 retrieve + light rerank (quantized int8) should keep rerank latency under 150ms on our Dedicated pools for batch=1 (we’ll validate p95).

Cost framing:
- We’ll produce a per-100k-query cost table that includes: embedding generation (per-vector compute), vector storage (per-month), index maintenance, egress (if you host embeddings with hyperscaler), plus rerank compute.

Next actions from Redwood (what we’ll do after we get your sample):
- Run embedding generation for 3 dims (512/768/1024) with our open model variants.
- Build HNSW and IVF indices and run retrieval latency matrix (batch=1,8,32).
- Run rerank pipeline on top-100 and measure end-to-end latency and recall@10/100.
- Deliver a single spreadsheet with recall/latency/cost comparisons and recommended config.

I’ll own the benchmarking scripts. If you can drop the S3 link (or upload to the Drive link Marissa sent), I’ll start the runs Thursday as soon as we have the sample.

—Ben
